name: Malaysia

facts.religion: Sunni Islam about 64%, Buddhist about 19%, Christian about 9%, Hindu about 6%

system_note: A federal monarchy whose king rotates among nine state rulers.
snapshot: Anwar Ibrahim's unity government faces corruption rows and ethnic tension ahead of an election due by early 2027.
culture: Malaysia's Malay, Chinese and Indian communities each keep their own festivals, cuisines and languages, and "open house" visits during Hari Raya, Chinese New Year and Deepavali bring them together. Hawker food, from nasi lemak to char kway teow, is a shared passion. Its king is chosen every five years from nine hereditary sultans.
society: Malaysia is a major hub for chip packaging and testing, and exports palm oil and gas. Policies favouring ethnic Malays, known as bumiputera, have shaped politics since 1971. The 1MDB scandal, in which billions were looted from a state fund, sent former prime minister Najib Razak to prison.
situation: In 2015 investigators found that some $4.5 billion had been looted from 1MDB, a state investment fund, with $700 million landing in the personal bank account of Prime Minister Najib Razak. It became one of the biggest financial scandals in history, helped topple the party that had ruled Malaysia since independence, and in 2022 put Najib in prison. That same year, Anwar Ibrahim, the reformer who had himself been jailed twice on charges widely seen as political, finally became prime minister after 25 years of trying, but only by allying with Najib's party, UMNO. In 2026 that bargain is coming due.

With a general election due by early 2027, Anwar's unity government is beset by corruption controversies, ethnic tensions and unease among both Malay and Chinese voters (East Asia Forum). Najib, 73, his sentence already halved by a royal pardon board in 2024, has kept fighting to serve the rest under house arrest, citing a disputed royal addendum. In September, as UMNO held its annual assembly, the pardons board met again to consider it; Anwar was reportedly upset not to have been told in advance, and the law minister and attorney general were said to oppose more clemency (The Vibes). For Anwar, freeing Najib would shred his anti-corruption credentials; refusing would anger the coalition partner he needs. Sabah and Sarawak, the resource-rich states on Borneo, are pressing for more autonomy and oil revenue, and Malaysia's electronics exports still face a 19 percent US tariff.
power: A federal constitutional monarchy. The king is chosen every five years in rotation from nine hereditary state rulers and holds limited but real powers, including pardons. The prime minister leads the coalition with a majority in the 222-seat lower house.
holders: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim (PKR), since 2022; King Sultan Ibrahim of Johor.
